scope: Each experiment uses one matched runner and one immutable cbfeb AOT package. No timings, frame distributions, percentiles, or ratios are pooled across jobs or source snapshots.
The persistent control and old composite bridge both use retained RGBA texture upload. The old composite mode here is distinct from the later legacy-composite mode using the original Uno uploader.

Raster-coverage Graphite requests effective sample count one. Both measured pan and zoom pass the unchanged native timing gate but are slower in wall time despite much lower active renderer-thread CPU.

The composite hover and selection gains compare against persistent within this snapshot. They do not establish recovery against the original 96e baseline and must not be multiplied by a ratio from another job.
Six primary samples determine each comparison. Two instrumented diagnostic runs are separate and excluded from all primary medians and ratios.

The three before/after/restored native pairs in each trial cover the Welcome timing fixture at DPR1. Broader Welcome lifecycle, fractional-DPR, and extended-SVG qualification belong to separate evidence and are not inferred from these 36 pairs.
ThreadTime measures active renderer main-thread CPU and excludes GPU and worker CPU. TaskDuration is elapsed task time and can include waits.

Offered operations per second and completed callbacks/submissions are not displayed frames or proven input-to-new-pixels latency. The input-tail checks only establish the existing observer's later-callback and graphics contracts.

All primary windows exclude startup, full warmup, screenshots, restore validation, and queue drains. Total experiment duration includes those phases plus separate diagnostics; it must not be replaced by a sum of primary windows.

Graphite drains asynchronously await previously submitted shared-queue work after measurement. The other bridge modes have no matched drain metric; these observations do not prove physical presentation or isolate GPU execution time.

Upload call counts and supplied JavaScript buffer bytes are API observations, not measured physical transfer bytes. Raw reports, console logs, renderer state, and all PNGs remain bound by the original artifact digests.
